meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'here is; (emphasis) that's', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: All right, here you go. There, look.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'here', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: The white one? Give me the keys.

examples.text: Мы сюда зачем прилетели? Я сразу сказал: с ним ничего не получится.
examples.trans: What did we even fly out here for? I said from the start: nothing will come of it with him.
Why did you even come here? Empty-handed!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'I', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'мотреть'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to look, to watch', paired with 'посмотреть'.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'to you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?
And this is for you. A toy car!

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('glad').

examples.trans: I'm very glad to see you.

examples.text: Ну что ты? Я очень рад тебя видеть.
examples.trans: Oh, come on! I'm very glad to see you.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'what', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to come, to arrive', paired with 'приходить'.

examples.trans: Security will be here any moment.

examples.text: Не надо, Самсон. Сейчас придёт охрана.
examples.trans: Don't, Samson. Security will be here any second.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'how; as', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'by the way; handy', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Oh, by the way, I almost forgot.

examples.text: Кстати, если хочешь, иди к нам в команду. Шансы у нас огромные.
examples.trans: By the way, if you want, join our team. Our chances are huge.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and, but; so', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'знать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to recognise; to find out', paired with 'узнавать'.

examples.trans: I'll find out where he is.
You recognised me. Thanks for seeing me.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'here', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'казать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to say, to tell', paired with 'говорить'.

examples.trans: Tell us, when will your programme be out?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'in, into', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'what; what a', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: Derived noun with agent/object suffix '-ник'/'-щик'/'-чик'. Common feminine noun meaning 'hospital' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Everyone thinks you're in the hospital.
He was admitted to the hospital.

examples.text: Все думают, ты в больнице. Откуда деньги?
examples.trans: Everyone thinks you're in the hospital. Where did the money come from?

лежать.gloss: to lie, to be lying down

meanings.en: to lie, to be lying down
meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to lie, to be lying down', paired with 'полежать'.

examples.trans: But I'll be lying next to Grishka for eternity.
The book is lying on the table.

examples.text: Телевизор мне смотреть недолго. А с Гришкой лежать вечность.
examples.trans: I won't be watching TV for much longer. But I'll be lying next to Grishka for eternity.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to know'.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'so, then; like that', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: So I shouldn't wait for you?
So I shouldn't wait for you tonight?

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'чему').

examples.trans: Why are we going so slowly?

examples.text: Виталик, почему мы так медленно едем? Быстрее!
examples.trans: Vitalik, why are we going so slowly? Faster!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'at, by; (у меня) I have', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'coffee machine' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Do not touch the coffee machine!

examples.text: И больше никогда не трогай кофемашину!
examples.trans: And never touch the coffee machine again!
Chef, the coffee machine broke down too.

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('dirty').

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to fine, penalize', paired with 'оштрафовать'.

examples.trans: The director fines the dishonest cook.

examples.text: Я штрафую тебя на двести тысяч рублей.
examples.trans: I am fining you two hundred thousand rubles.

examples.text: А ещё я сегодня вас штрафую!
examples.trans: And furthermore, I am fining you today!

meanings.note: Prefix 'во-' ('into, up') marks inward or upward movement (stem 'обще').

examples.trans: I have no idea at all.

examples.text: Я человек чистый. Я вообще не вор.
examples.trans: I'm an honest man. I'm not a thief at all.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.
Common masculine noun meaning 'coffee' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Какое хорошее утро! Лидия Алексеевна, чашку кофе, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: What a lovely morning! Lidia Alekseyevna, a cup of coffee, please.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'делать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to do, to make', paired with 'делать'.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'where', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: А где машинка? Где моя машинка?
examples.trans: Hey, where's the toy car? Where's my toy car?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'everything, all; that's it', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Мы просто не хотели вас беспокоить. Всё отменим!
examples.trans: We just didn't want to bother you. We'll cancel it all!

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'oranges' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Я принёс свежие апельсины к бару.
examples.trans: I brought fresh oranges to the bar.

examples.text: Вот и занимайся своими апельсинами на кухне!
examples.trans: Then attend to your oranges in the kitchen!

meanings.note: Common neuter noun meaning 'wine' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: And what about the wine and fruit?

examples.text: Смотри, это электрогитара для Лёши. А тебе я взял чилийское вино и ягоды.
examples.trans: Look, this is an electric guitar for Lyosha. And for you I brought Chilean wine and berries.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'казать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to order', paired with 'заказывать'.

examples.text: Если опоздают, пицца бесплатно. Может, закажем?
examples.trans: If they're late, the pizza is free. Maybe we should order?
